name: Pomeranian Voivodeship
summary_text: No voivodeship-level trans-specific resolution, incident series or enforcement finding was located for this division in the current research pass. The anti-LGBT municipal-resolution wave (80+ municipalities and four voivodeship-level declarations as of March 2020) concentrated in the eastern and south-eastern parts of the country, so the absence of local findings here indicates thinner documentation rather than established safety. The national frame governs this division: no hate-crime protection on sexual-orientation or gender-identity grounds (the March 2025 amendment bill referred to the Constitutional Tribunal, hearings held July and September 2025), court-based and medically gatekept legal gender recognition, and national sources documenting a trans foreign woman held in a male-only guarded detention centre and an ECtHR ruling that denying a prisoner hormone therapy violates private life.

sources.title: Transgender woman released from a guarded center for male foreigners - Association for Legal Intervention
sources.claim_summary: Legal-aid NGO report (13-28 March 2024): a Polish regional court placed a Vietnamese trans woman, taking hormones since 2018, in a guarded detention centre for male foreigners; the Border Guard refused to move her or to deliver her medication, interrupting her hormone therapy for three months; she was released after the NGO's application citing health grounds (Act on Foreigners, Art. 406(1) with 400(1)).

sources.title: ECtHR rules Polish prison authorities violated trans woman's rights by denying access to hormone therapy - TGEU - Trans Europe and Central AsiaTGEU – Trans Europe and Central Asia
sources.claim_summary: TGEU report (16 July 2024): on 11 July the ECtHR held that Polish prison authorities violated the right to private and family life by denying a trans woman access to hormone replacement therapy while imprisoned (she had been prescribed hormones for almost two years; Siedlce prison gave no reasonable grounds for refusal); EUR 8,000 damages ordered; TGEU intervened in 2021; part of a growing Council of Europe standard on trans prisoners' healthcare.
